findings: The November canonical page gives the card-brand filtering purpose and three platform routes. The April 22 full guide includes all three variants with configuration, prerequisites and example tests (old raw lines 1-180, new raw lines 1-15). The old filename year is not the capture date.

April requires a Stripe account and an integrated Mobile Payment Element and shows PaymentSheet cardBrandAcceptance allow/disallow choices. Allowed admits only listed brands, while disallowed excludes listed brands. The supported examples use Visa, Mastercard, Amex and Discover. Discover is the Discover Global Network group including Discover, Diners Club, JCB, UnionPay and Elo. iOS and React Native cover card form and Apple Pay, and Android covers card form and Google Pay (old raw lines 12-48, 63-113 and 127-169).

The iOS property sits on PaymentSheet.Configuration with Swift brand categories, Android uses PaymentSheet.Configuration.Builder and PaymentSheet.CardBrandAcceptance.BrandCategory, and React Native passes filter and brands into initPaymentSheet. The Android sample presents the sheet with a PaymentIntent client secret and the configuration. A permitted card or supported wallet establishes neither confirmed payment nor capture. The old test card instructions concern Mobile Payment Element acceptance or blocking, and the rendered failure screenshots are historical references (old raw lines 33-57, 84-121 and 148-180).

The existing source lines 13-50 directly represent the April choices, group mapping and most option shapes. It does not label the historical variants, show the Mobile Payment Element integration prerequisite, or distinguish client filtering from server-side confirmation and unsupported Link behavior in separately retained declarations.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-mobile-filter-card-brands-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-inapp-filter-card-brands-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-filter-card-brands.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/filter-card-brands`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/filter-card-brands, the November capture establishes the card-brand filtering purpose and routes to iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-15). The mapped source-stripe-inapp-filter-card-brands.md summarizes the April full guide. That guide assumes a Stripe account and Mobile Payment Element integration. PaymentSheet cardBrandAcceptance can allow only listed brands or exclude listed brands through platform-specific configuration. It covers the card form on all three platforms, Apple Pay in the iOS and React Native variants, and Google Pay in the Android variant. Visa, Mastercard, Amex and Discover are categories, with Discover covering Discover, Diners Club, JCB, UnionPay and Elo. Android sets the configuration when presenting with a PaymentIntent client secret. React Native uses initPaymentSheet and the filter and brands properties. This is client UI selection evidence, distinct from creating or confirming a payment, and the suggested test card checks concern acceptance or blocking in the UI (old raw lines 12-57, old raw lines 63-121 and old raw lines 127-180). The summary preserves the core choices and shapes but needs the historical, platform and client scope explicit.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/filter-card-brands, the November change is navigation-only. The purpose remains and the three variant URLs take the place of the April variant bodies (new raw lines 5-15). Keep the dated allow and disallow example shapes, Discover Global Network grouping, platform wallet coverage, prerequisites and test references in source-stripe-inapp-filter-card-brands.md (old raw lines 12-57, old raw lines 63-121 and old raw lines 127-180). Warn reciprocally that the Swift source joins two statements and the React Native fragment joins a comment and omits an enum namespace import. Keep the configured client filter distinct from the separate server ConfirmationToken/PaymentIntent flow. The separately retained exact SDK declarations call this client-side and exclude Link within their version scope, with a separate default All in the React Native contract. The neighboring EmbeddedPaymentElement route uses a different iOS configuration namespace and has Android wallet prose inconsistent with this PaymentSheet guide. Preserve the surface distinction without extending the Android Apple Pay wording to PaymentSheet or runtime. The November index does not verify current SDK ranges, wallet behavior, server-side enforcement or any live payment outcome.
